title: What I learnt from Beatrix Potter
html:
Flicking through the channels on Sunday night, I started watching Miss Potter. What caught my attention most was that when she looked at her drawings, they came to life. She talked to them and they moved and interacted with her.

I liked that because it was a visual explanation of how her stories came to life for her, as she painted and wrote, almost telling themselves.

The real Potter was, and is, an inspiration to millions. I like the fact that even in stuffy Victorian times there was someone with so vivid an imagination that she was able to do what she wanted to, in spite of the times.

By being a "woman of means" she was able to get out from under her parents rule, follow her passion, and change the world. And she was able to do that without the internet, without a cell phone or a Blackberry, without Google and under social rules that precluded woman from having a brain.

Miss Potter did all she did without the freedoms we enjoy today. So, what’s your excuse for not doing all you can and want to do?
